final_answer:
**Underwriting Analysis**

**DTI**: 29.92% — well under the 50% DU limit (B3-6-02).  
**Credit score**: 704 — no minimum for DU; well above 620 (B3-5.1-01).  
**LTV**: 80% (220,000/275,000).  
**Funds to close**: $62,130 (down payment $55,000 + closing costs $7,130).  
**Available funds**: Bank balance $59,830 + $22,000 gift = $81,830.  
**Reserves**: 11.16 months after closing — no minimum required for 1-unit principal residence (B3-4.1-01).  
**No bankruptcy/foreclosure** — clean credit history.

**Critical issue**: The $22,000 gift is from an "interested party" with a gift letter. Per B3-4.3-04, personal gifts cannot come from interested parties (builder, developer, real estate agent, or any other party to the transaction). This must be treated as an Interested Party Contribution (IPC) under B3-4.1-02.

For principal residence at 80% LTV (75.01%–90% range), maximum financing concessions = 6% of property value ($16,500), but limited to actual closing costs ($7,130). The borrower’s own funds ($59,830) fall $2,300 short of the $62,130 cash to close. The IPC can cover this $2,300 shortfall as a financing concession (within the $7,130 limit). The remaining $19,700 of the $22,000 becomes a sales concession, reducing the effective sales price to $255,300 (LTV 86.2%).

The file fails the gift requirement without reclassification. With proper IPC treatment, the borrower has sufficient funds to close.

DECISION: approve with conditions  
RULES: B3-4.3-04, B3-4.1-02
